thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Multiple 5xx and egress failures detected - high severity. Affected: service-app-prod in az-east-3. Pager triggered at 2026-03-15T10:02:00Z. Linked runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/egress-failure
micah: on it. grabbing logs and checking recent infra changes. assigning to network on-call. @oncall-net can you take?
oncall-net: taking. i see alerts for NAT gateway errors and route propagation anomalies. starting live triage.
sofia: seeing increased TCP resets and destination unreachable from app nodes in az-east-3. graph: 5xx spike at 10:00, egress errors from nat-gw-a1 at 10:01.
lee: FYI there was a terraform apply 9m ago that touched route-table associations for the private subnets in az-east-3. change: added tag egress-owner=team-alpha and associated rt-0a1b2c to subnet-priv-az3.
anika: pulling terraform plan from CI. commit id 9f3b2d. snippet:
```
resource aws_route_table_association "private_az3" {
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.private_az3.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.app_egress.id
}
```
this looks normal but the target route table appears to point at a route that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to a cross-az NAT in az-east-2 instead of the local nat-gw.
micah: that would explain partial impact and latency increase. approx what fraction of subnets are associated wrong?
sofia: quick calc from describe-route-tables: 3 of 10 private subnets in az-east-3 now point to rt-0a1b2c which has default-route -> nat-gw-b (in az-east-2). so ~30% of traffic from az-east-3 app nodes hitting cross-az nat.
lee: terraform applied with wrong variable interpolation for map of rt ids. blame: ambiguous map key. i'll stop the CI run and start rollback of that module.
deploy-bot: terraform: detect drift - initiating targeted rollback for module network.private_az_bindings at 10:08Z.
anika: mitigation idea: re-associate those 3 subnets back to the previous route table rt-0f9e8d which points to nat-gw-a1. can do that with aws cli quickly. also consider creating a temporary nat in az-east-3 to relieve cross-az egress.
oncall-net: agree. re-assoc first, then monitor. micah can you coordinate with security for any transient IGW exposure? we want to avoid leaking to public.
micah: noted. will grant minimal window and watch subnets' route propagation.
sofia: running associate command now:
```
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-0abc123 --route-table-id rt-0f9e8d
```
returns association updated for subnet-priv-az3a. repeating for the other two.
sofia: update: all 3 subnets re-associated to rt-0f9e8d. packets starting to egress via local nat-gw-a1 again. seeing drop in 5xx within 30s. :thumbsup:
micah: great. any terraform state changes to prevent this from happening on next apply?
lee: yes we'll pin the map keys and add a validation check in CI: ensure route_table_id for each az matches nat-gw id in same az. i will open a PR.
anika: adding temporary alert rule to warn if cross-az egress exceeds 5% of traffic for an AZ.
sofia: traffic and error curves look back to baseline. still seeing a small tail. running packet captures to validate TCP flows.
carmen: support: we have a few customers reporting elevated latencies and some 502s between 10:00-10:12. estimated impacted customers: 4. tier2 prepping customer notes.
support-bot: created ticket INC-11234 and linked to status page incident 32345. drafting post-incident note.
oncall-net: handing off to network next-shift, assigning follow-ups: 1) PR to CI to validate rt<->nat mapping, 2) postmortem and list of affected subnets, 3) verify terraform variable typing. summary to hand off: misapplied rt associations via terraform introduced cross-az nat egress for ~3 subnets in az-east-3 causing 5xx and latency. initial mitigation: manual re-association to rt-0f9e8d at 10:09-10:11.
micah: thanks. @oncall-net you have run of show, i'll leave monitoring and customer communications with @carmen. please update channel with postmortem link when ready.
oncall-net: taking the handoff. open actions noted. i'll run a secondary sweep for any other terraform-applied route changes across regions.
micah: closing pager, thanks everyone for fast response :star: 
incident-bot: Incident closed for active paging. timeline summary: alert 10:02 -> mitigation 10:09 -> service recovery 10:12 -> handoff 10:15. See runbook link for full timeline.
carmen: will post customer impact email draft in #support-distro in 30m and attach impact numbers.
micah: adding postmortem owner: lee. please include recommended CI checks and an ops runbook step for quick re-association.
lee: will do. ETA for draft postmortem: EOD today.
notes: severity: high; impact: partial egress and latency for subset of app nodes in az-east-3; root cause: terraform route-table association misconfiguration; mitigated via manual re-association and targeted rollback.
